verdict.rationale: dLocal's docs say merchants that are not fully PCI DSS compliant should collect card data through Smart Fields or use Checkout Redirect, and can then rely on dLocal's PCI Level 1 status and complete the relevant SAQ. Saved cards are charged by `card_id`, a token-style reference. The evidence never explicitly says raw card data bypasses merchant servers or which reduced SAQ applies, so scope reduction is implied rather than fully documented. missing for 10: an explicit statement that card data never touches merchant servers when using Smart Fields, documentation of the reduced SAQ type (e.g., SAQ A/A-EP), detail on how Smart Fields tokenizes cards, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep my systems out of most of PCI DSS scope because card data is tokenized and never touches my servers

citations.quote: If your business is not Full PCI DSS compliant, you need to securely collect the card information using Smart Fields.
if you are using dLocal you will rely on our PCI Level 1 status and complete the relevant SAQ.
For recurring payments, first save the card, and then use the `card_id` to charge the card.
you can process payments safely and simply with a ready-to-use design and front end. Learn more about Checkout Redirect.
